definition.simple: The new substance made when an acid and a base cancel each other out.
definition.academic: A compound formed by the neutralization reaction between an acid and a base. Salts can be acidic, basic, or neutral in nature.

common_misconceptions: Salt only means the white table salt we eat. (Correction: In science, 'salt' is a general category for any substance formed by neutralizing an acid and a base.)
ai_context.tutor_hint: Remind the student that there are many types of salts in chemistry, and table salt (Sodium Chloride) is just one specific example.
